facts.t: No Indian judge has ever been removed by impeachment
facts.d: Justice V. Ramaswami's motion failed in 1993 when the ruling party abstained. Justice Soumitra Sen and Justice Dinakaran both resigned before the process concluded. The mechanism exists on paper and has never once reached its end.

facts.t: Investigating a judge requires the Chief Justice's permission
facts.d: K. Veeraswami (1991) held that no criminal investigation against a sitting judge may begin without prior sanction from the Chief Justice of India — a protection that has no counterpart for any other public servant.

facts.t: 8,630 complaints against judges in nine years
facts.d: That figure, given in a ministerial reply to Parliament, covers 2016 to 2025. The in-house procedure that handles them has no statutory backing, no timelines and no requirement to disclose outcomes.

bank.q: With reference to the removal of a judge, consider the following statements:
s: A motion requires 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members.
A three-member committee inquires into the charges.
Removal requires a two-thirds majority in both Houses.
bank.e: All three are correct, under Articles 124(4) and 217(1)(b) read with the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.

bank.q: Independence of the judiciary was recognised as part of the basic structure in:
bank.e: The Second Judges Case of 1994, which also established judicial primacy in appointments.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a structural component of judicial independence?
o: Salaries charged on the Consolidated Fund and not variable to a judge's disadvantage
Collegium primacy in appointments and transfers
Prior permission of the Chief Justice before investigating a judge
bank.e: That protection, from K. Veeraswami, is classified under institutional accountability mechanisms rather than structural independence.

bank.q: Match List I (provision) with List II (subject):
pairs: 1. High Court control over the subordinate judiciary
2. Bar on discussing a judge's conduct in legislatures except on impeachment
3. Salaries not variable to a judge's disadvantage
bank.e: Articles 121 and 211 restrict legislative discussion, Article 235 gives High Courts control over the district judiciary, Articles 129 and 215 confer contempt power, and Articles 125 and 221 protect salaries.

bank.as: Resignation operates as a loophole in judicial accountability.
bank.rs: Investigations lapse once a judge leaves office, so findings are never published.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — hence the proposal that inquiries continue and conclusions be published even after resignation.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about asset disclosure by judges:
s: It rests on a Supreme Court resolution of 1997.
Mandatory statutory disclosure is among the proposed reforms.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The 1997 resolution is voluntary, not binding — which is why mandatory disclosure keeps being proposed.

bank.q: All of the following are identified as problems with the accountability framework EXCEPT:
o: The absence of intermediate sanctions short of removal
The in-house procedure's lack of statutory backing
An excess of statutory timelines constraining inquiry
Susceptibility of the removal process to political derailment
bank.e: There are no timelines at all — their absence is what allows evasion by delay.

bank.q: Which foreign body is cited as a model for an independent judicial oversight mechanism?
o: The United Kingdom's Judicial Conduct Investigations Office
The European Court of Human Rights
bank.e: The JCIO, alongside European and Latin American judicial councils. India's own attempt, the Judicial Standards and Accountability Bill of 2010, lapsed.

bank.q: With reference to transparency, consider the following as areas where confidentiality remains justified:
s: Internal judicial deliberations and draft judgments.
Principles governing case listing and bench allocation.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Listing and bench-allocation principles are listed among the areas where greater transparency is justified.

bank.q: Which American institution issues reprimands and suspensions as intermediate judicial sanctions?
o: The Judicial Councils of the Circuits
bank.e: The Judicial Councils of the Circuits, which can reprimand, suspend case assignments, or refer a judge for impeachment — the graduated response India lacks.

bank.as: Independence without accountability risks becoming judicial supremacy.
bank.rs: Accountability without independence risks becoming political subordination.
bank.e: Both statements are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion — it states the opposite danger. Together they define the balance constitutional morality requires.

bank.q: Consider the following case studies in judicial accountability:
s: Justice V. Ramaswami's impeachment failed owing to political abstentions.
Justice Dinakaran resigned on the day of the inquiry.
Justice Soumitra Sen was successfully removed by both Houses.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Justice Sen resigned before the process was completed — no judge has ever been removed to the end of the procedure.
